questions.q: Antibodies in our body are complex:
questions.explain: Antibodies (immunoglobulins) are glycoproteins produced in response to antigens.
questions.voice_q: First one. Antibodies in our body are complex what? Five seconds... think!
questions.voice_a: It's A — glycoproteins. Antibodies are immunoglobulins, made of protein plus sugar chains.

questions.q: A patient has internal bleeding, muscle pain, fever, anaemia, and a blocked intestine. Most likely disease?
questions.explain: Ascariasis, caused by the roundworm Ascaris, blocks the intestine and causes these symptoms.
questions.voice_q: A patient has internal bleeding, muscle pain, fever, anaemia, and a blocked intestine. Which disease? Go!
questions.voice_a: The answer is C — Ascariasis. The roundworm Ascaris blocks the intestine and triggers all of these.

questions.q: An antibody's light and heavy chains are joined by disulphide bonds. These bonds form between:
questions.explain: Disulphide bonds form between two cysteine residues — the only amino acid with a free thiol group.
questions.voice_q: Last one. An antibody's chains are joined by disulphide bonds. Between which amino acids? Five seconds!
questions.voice_a: It's D — cysteine and cysteine. Only cysteine has the sulphur group that forms a disulphide bridge.
